sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: os.Getenv(key) → string (empty if unset), os.LookupEnv(key) → (value, ok — distinguishes unset from empty), os.Setenv(key, value), os.Environ() → all.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The functions, executed:

```go
os.Setenv("MYVAR", "hello")

os.Getenv("MYVAR")      // "hello" — verified
os.Getenv("NOTSET")     // "" — same as an empty var: ambiguous
os.LookupEnv("MYVAR")  // ("hello", true) — present
os.LookupEnv("NOTSET") // ("", false) — ABSENT — the distinction
```

The two reading forms:
Getenv returns a string — empty for unset AND empty-set (you can't tell). LookupEnv returns (string, bool) — the bool is 'was it set' — the form for when empty-vs-unset matters (an empty DATABASE_URL might mean 'use a default'; an unset one might mean 'not configured — fail').

The convention: config values live in env vars (12-factor). The pattern:
```go
if v, ok := os.LookupEnv("PORT"); ok {
    port = v
} else {
    port = "8080"  // default
}
```

Setting: os.Setenv — process-local (the process's environment; doesn't affect the parent or siblings). Useful for testing (set up an env-dependent function's input) and for child-process configuration (os/exec inherits the current process's environment).

The type discipline: env vars are strings — numbers need strconv.Atoi(port), time.ParseDuration(d.Timeout), URLs url.Parse — with the error handling that goes with parsing.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[os.Environ] --> V[os.Getenv key]
    V --> S[string — empty if unset]
    L[os.LookupEnv key] --> D[(string, bool — set?)]
    SET[os.Setenv] --> P[process env — children inherit]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The environment inheritance model: a Go process starts with the parent's environment (the shell's exported variables, the container's ENV, the Kubernetes configMap's entries). Setenv mutates the process's own copy — children (exec.Command) inherit it, parents don't see it. The lifecycle: process-local, no persistence.

The Environ() inventory: os.Environ() returns a []string of KEY=VALUE pairs — the complete environment. The pattern for debugging and for filtering (find all MYAPP_*-prefixed vars). The companion: os.ExpandEnv("$HOME/dir") — shell-style expansion within a string.

The godotenv pattern (the .env convention): the library loads a .env file into the process's env at startup — the dev-time convenience that the container's ENV directives replace in production. The pattern to know: the APP reads env vars (never the .env file directly); the loading is a startup step (main or init) — the config flow stays env-var-shaped.
